requirements.quote: An obligation requires `source_type`, `source_ref` and an anchor (or `manual`), description, owner, due date (nullable only for undated tasks) and status; creation without provenance is rejected.

A DB check plus service guard enforce that status `closed` requires a `closed_reason` in (`completed_task`, `lawyer_action`, `not_applicable`) and, for `not_applicable`, non-empty reason text; a direct SQL update violating this fails.

`reconcileOrder(orderId)` returns the order's directions each marked `obligation`, `not_applicable` (with reason) or `unresolved`; an order is `reconciled` only when no direction is unresolved, and the unresolved count feeds brief readiness (#60).
Proposed obligations from extraction (#46) arrive as L2 proposals; confirming creates the obligation with the original anchor and records the confirmer.

Defects: `raiseDefect` creates a defect obligation with a cure deadline and moves the proceeding to `defects`; `representFiling` moves to `re_presented`; allocation of SR (Madras) or FR (Karnataka) numbers is stored on the proceeding without implying court status.
Certified copies move through applied -> ready -> collected, each transition dated and sourced, and surface in the queue as obligations with a follow-up reminder.

`queryQueue` groups obligations as `overdue`, `today`, `this_week`, `later`, `undated`, filterable by matter, owner, kind and source; overdue sort first by age; p95 < 150 ms on the seeded dataset and one query per group.
Rescheduling an obligation requires a reason, preserves history in `obligation_event`, and is distinguished from a miss in the missed-obligation metric (deliberate reschedule is not a miss).
Reminders: a job emits in-app reminders for obligations due within the member's lead time and overdue obligations once per day; idempotent; delivery via #23.

Roles: owner and advocate manage all; junior manages assigned matters; clerk can manage tasks, defects and copies but not strategy notes; viewer read-only. All checked by `can()` and covered by tests.
Every mutation writes an `audit_event`; undo of an L3 task creation cascades correctly (#47 contract).
Obligation due dates are never computed from a generated legal rule; rule-driven limitation dates live in #84 behind a flag.
Cross-tenant tests pass: a user in workspace A cannot read or mutate this feature's rows in workspace B via SQL, service, server action or API, including a user who belongs to both.
Every new tenant table has `workspace_id uuid not null`, an RLS policy using `app.workspace_id`, and is covered by the CI cross-tenant suite.
Inputs are validated with zod schemas from `packages/validators`; no `any` appears in exported types.
Strategy-bearing descriptions are hidden from clerks via column-scoped views.
requirements.why: The obligation table has no strategy-note column or flag to scope on; defining one (and the clerk view) is a product/schema decision separate from the service. Clerk role rules in R10 are still delivered.
